approach: Test-side changes in crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs: replace the firstmate-only constants (STUDY_SHA, study_dir(), mounted_tree(), STUDY_FILES) with a per-directory `check_study(dir, pin_env, mount) -> Vec<String>` and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount)` that walks every `studies/*/`. The kept test reads ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA from the process environment and passes them in as arguments, so tests never set env vars (the workspace denies unsafe_code). For every directory it checks the conventions (no placeholders, 40-hex pin, every source SHA equals the pin via the existing `wrong_sha` rule with a `NoTree` lookup, every claim text starts `[mechanism]` or `[prose-only]`, a "none" guard is never code-evaluated and has no counters, pin/validation study_id equals the directory name). Only when the pin's URL and SHA equal the env pair and a mount exists does it run `validate()` and require `computed == validation.json`. A pin with the same URL but a different SHA fails naming the study id. Fault tests run on tempfile copies. A hermetic test rebuilds a tree from each study's own citations so the full-validation route runs in a plain checkout; the rebuilt tree (revised for finding 1) collects every quote cited at a line and joins quotes that share a line with a space, pads with blank lines to the highest cited end line, and the test first requires `bad-citation` and `quote-mismatch` to pass on that tree before comparing with validation.json. `Study::admit` in lib.rs also refuses a change spanning two `studies/<id>/` directories and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md. The study producer prompt states the conventions, the one-directory rule and (finding 3) that a claim quote stays verbatim even if the scan list holds one of its words, rewritten so the study set grows by no more than 25 tokens (about 75 bytes net) and docs/system-facts.md stays untouched. xtask/tests/policy.rs gets `boundary_scan_file(path, text)`, which blanks only claim-source `quote` values in `studies/<id>/claims.json` before word matching and always matches machine-path fragments on the raw text. Planted terms are split strings joined at run time. A CHANGELOG entry is added and `tempfile` becomes a dev-dependency of the study crate.

decisions.choice: Pass the pin env pair and the mount path to `check_study` as arguments; only the kept test reads `std::env::var`.
decisions.reason: The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "deny"` (Cargo.toml line 59), so tests cannot call `set_var`. Arguments let temp-copy tests exercise every pin case in parallel without touching process state.

rejected.why: Needs unsafe in edition 2024 and races with parallel tests.

rejected.option: Run a child `cargo test` with env set
rejected.why: Slow, and the verifier may run only whole simple cargo commands.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing `wrong_sha` rule (rules.rs:264-289), run with a `NoTree` GitLookup that answers nothing, as the check for a source SHA that differs from the pin. The offending id is the owner id the rule already reports.
decisions.reason: `wrong_sha` only compares strings and never calls git for file sources, so it works with no tree. This avoids a second SHA comparison that could drift.

rejected.option: Re-implement the SHA comparison in the test
rejected.why: Duplicates logic that can drift from the rule.

decisions.choice: Put the convention checks in the `#[cfg(test)]` module of rules.rs, as the kept test is today; `RULES` (18 rules) is unchanged.
decisions.reason: The request names the kept test in rules.rs. The conventions are repository policy over study data, not part of the validation core, and adding rules would change validation.json for firstmate, which may not change.

rejected.why: This would change firstmate's validation.json, and nothing under studies/firstmate-work-handling/ may change.

decisions.choice: With no mount, env unset, or env naming another URL, check conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and SHA but no mount, conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and a different SHA, fail naming the study id whether or not a mount exists. (Finding 4: the rule is kept as the request asks; the conflict with several studies of one repository is recorded as a user open question and in the CHANGELOG entry.)
decisions.reason: This is the request's rule. A mismatch is a fault in pin.json or in the pinning, never a reason to validate quietly against the wrong tree. crates/athena-core/src/run/pin.rs `study_pin` (lines 82-133) lets several studies share one URL and picks one by the study id in the request; under this rule a job on study B with ATHENA_PIN_SHA from B makes study A (same URL, other SHA) fail the kept test. The environment pair carries no study id, so the test cannot tell which study was chosen. The user decides whether to relax it.

rejected.option: Validate any mounted tree against every study
rejected.why: A second study would fail its own quote checks against firstmate's tree.

rejected.option: Compare only the study the pinning step picked
rejected.why: ATHENA_PIN_* carries only URL and SHA (no study id) and no code in the snapshot sets the pair; the request says match on URL and SHA.

rejected.option: Skip a same-URL different-SHA study silently
rejected.why: The acceptance criterion requires a failure naming the id for that case.

decisions.choice: Admission: collect `studies/<id>/...` ids over all non-build-output paths. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Every path that is not build output, not exactly `CHANGELOG.md` at the root and not under `studies/<id>/` gives a `study-outside-directory` violation. Paths with `.`, `..` or empty segments, and a bare `studies/<name>` file, count as outside.
decisions.reason: Matches the brief. Build-output paths keep their existing single `build-output` violation, so `build_output_is_refused` (lib.rs:187) still sees exactly one violation.

rejected.option: Also flag build output as outside the directory
rejected.why: Gives two violations for one path and breaks the existing test.

rejected.option: Allow `studies/README.md` or files directly under studies/
rejected.why: They belong to no study id, and the brief says exactly one directory.

decisions.choice: The boundary exemption blanks only the string values of `sources[].quote` of the claims, and only in `studies/<id>/claims.json` (exactly one id segment). It parses with serde_json to collect the claim quote strings, then replaces `"quote": <literal>` pairs whose literal is in that set, keeping line numbers. Word matching runs on the blanked text, fragment matching on the raw text. If the file does not parse, nothing is exempt. `boundary_scan` stays unchanged so `the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` compares like with like.
decisions.reason: Exempts only text quoting studied source, keeps scanning prose and machine-path fragments.

rejected.option: Skip all of claims.json, or all of studies/
rejected.why: Would hide a claim's own prose and the rest of the study.
The request names the claims' quote fields; rationales.json stays fully scanned. Raised as a user question.

decisions.choice: Do not touch docs/system-facts.md. Write the study producer prompt so the study set grows by at most 25 tokens over its current 1018 (the largest producer set recorded there is 1043). Tighten existing bullets while adding the three conventions, the one-directory rule and the claim-quote clause (finding 3).
decisions.reason: docs/system-facts.md is not among the deliverables. `computed_rows()` in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs takes the maximum over capabilities, so a study set at or under 1043 leaves the recorded row unchanged. The size is checkable: `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails if the largest set moves.

rejected.option: Update the `- budget producer:` line in docs/system-facts.md when the set grows
rejected.why: The file is not a listed deliverable; the plan keeps the study set within the existing figure.
The facts file says to update the line, never the budget.

rejected.option: Drop the one-directory rule from the prompt
rejected.why: Admission refuses such changes, so the producer should be told the rule.

decisions.choice: Finding 3: the prompt gets a short clause, e.g. 'A claim quote stays verbatim even if it holds a scanned word; the scan skips claim quotes only.' It has lowest priority among the additions: if the three conventions plus the directory rule leave no room within 25 tokens, the clause is left out and the CHANGELOG entry names it as a known gap (producer briefs say never to write the scan's words in any file, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/boundary.rs:54-62, so a study producer may reword a quote and trip `quote-mismatch`).
decisions.reason: The exemption helps only if the producer knows to keep the quote verbatim. Both outcomes are covered: clause present, or gap recorded in the changelog; neither edits the facts file.

rejected.option: Edit boundary.rs to tell study producers the exception
rejected.why: Out of the deliverables; it is shared by every capability's brief.
The finding asks for the clause or a recorded gap.

decisions.choice: Finding 1: `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` builds each file as a vector of lines sized to the highest `end_line` cited for that path. For every file source it appends the quote to the line at `start_line`; where several quotes begin on the same line (firstmate has single-line ranges shared by several quotes) they are joined with a single space on that line. Every cited range then contains its own quote as a substring, which is all `quote_mismatch` (rules.rs:339-365) checks. Before comparing with validation.json the test requires `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` to report nothing on this tree, so a placement fault is named instead of surfacing as a diff.
decisions.reason: A file-per-path, one-quote-per-line layout collides on firstmate's data (docs/configuration.md 357-357 at claims.json lines 13-14, AGENTS.md 234-234, docs/agent-control.md 131-131, bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh 49-49, docs/configuration.md 1088-1088, bin/fm-spawn.sh 3165-3165). `cited_lines` (rules.rs:292-299) joins the lines of the range and only needs `end <= lines.len()`, so joining and padding are enough. Firstmate has no commit or run sources (grep of kind values in the study found none), and `MountedTree::reachable` is `commit == from`, so file sources are all the tree must hold.

rejected.option: One quote per line, panic on a collision
rejected.why: Panics on firstmate's real data, so the criterion 1 test would fail.

rejected.option: Place colliding quotes on neighbouring lines
rejected.why: A single-line range cites exactly one line, so the neighbour is outside the range.

decisions.choice: Finding 2: criterion 1's demonstration gives the exact command for a checkout that has pinned-source/ and states that this job's verifier cannot see that case.
decisions.reason: The mounted case is the only one that proves the quotes against the real tree; the hermetic tree proves only the route and the recorded equality.

rejected.option: Present the rebuilt-tree test as proof of the mounted case
rejected.why: It is built from the study's own citations, so it cannot show the real tree holds the quotes.

files.purpose: Replace the firstmate-only test section (from about line 1395) with generic helpers `NoTree`, `Loaded::read(dir)`, `conventions`, `check_study`, `check_studies`, `synthetic_tree` (shared-line quotes joined, padded to the highest end line), the kept test over every studies/*/ and the temp-copy fault tests. Non-test code is unchanged.
`admit()` also refuses a change spanning more than one studies/<id>/ and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md (build output keeps its own violation); add unit tests.

State the conventions: enforcement tags, no placeholders, a 'none' guard never checked by code, one studies/<id>/ plus CHANGELOG.md per job, and (room permitting) that claim quotes stay verbatim; tighten existing bullets so the study set grows by at most 25 tokens.
Split word and fragment scanning, add `boundary_scan_file` with the claim-quote exemption, use it in the tree scan, and add tests that plant split-string terms.

One entry under [Unreleased] / Changed describing the per-study validation, the prompt conventions, the admission rule, the boundary exemption, the several-studies-of-one-URL note and, if the prompt clause did not fit, the claim-quote gap.
Add `tempfile.workspace = true` to [dev-dependencies] for the temp-copy tests.
Add "tempfile" to the athena-cap-study dependency list so `--locked` passes.

steps: rules.rs, test module: remove `STUDY_SHA`, `study_dir()`, the firstmate-only `mounted_tree()` and `STUDY_FILES` as a fixed list (derive the file list from `studies/<dir>/`). Add `NoTree` (a GitLookup answering None/false), generalize `MountedTree::new(sha, root)`, and add `Loaded::read(dir) -> Result<Loaded, String>` (pin, claims, rationales, model, findings, validation) with `violations(git, rule)` and `validate(git)`.

rules.rs: add `conventions(dir, loaded) -> Vec<String>`. It checks: no 'UNRESOLVED' or 'not examined' (case-insensitive) in any study file; pin.sha is 40-hex; `wrong_sha` (via `NoTree`) reports no owner; every claim text starts '[mechanism] ' or '[prose-only] '; every transition with guard 'none' has `guard_evaluated_by != Code` and empty `guard_counters`; pin.study_id and validation.study_id equal the directory name; each file source has a non-blank quote. Every message starts with the offending id (claim, card, transition or study).

rules.rs: add `check_study(dir, pin_env: Option<(&str,&str)>, mount: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<String>` and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount)`, which sorts and walks directories under studies/ and fails if there are none. Rules: conventions always; if the env url equals pin.repository_url and the sha differs, a problem naming the study id and both SHAs; if url and sha equal and a mount exists, run `validate()` with `MountedTree`, report each failing rule with its offending ids, and report when `computed != validation.json`. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` reads the two env vars (non-empty), uses `../../pinned-source` if it is a directory, calls `check_studies` on `../../studies`, and prints for each study 'fully validated' or 'conventions only'.

rules.rs: add `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir`: for every path cited by a file source, a vector of lines sized to the highest end_line cited for that path (blank lines by default); for each source append its quote to the line at start_line, joining quotes that share a line with one space; write the lines joined by newline. Add the tests: `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations` (asserts `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` report nothing on the rebuilt tree first, then `validate()` equals validation.json), `a_study_that_breaks_a_convention_or_its_pin_fails_naming_the_id` (copy helper, JSON edits, four faults, control, conventions-only case), `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too`, and ports of the quote, SHA and range mutation checks from the old firstmate test using ids read from the data instead of the literals c1 and ra1. Before writing, Grep firstmate's claims.json for escaped newlines in quotes and for kinds other than file, and report if any exists.

lib.rs: add `fn study_dir_of(path) -> Option<&str>` (a `studies/<id>/<rest>` path whose segments are all plain, with a non-empty id and rest) and extend `admit()`. Build-output paths produce `build-output` as before and are skipped by the new checks. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Each other path that is not `CHANGELOG.md` and not under a study directory gives a `study-outside-directory` violation with its path. Add tests for the six cases in the criterion 3 demonstration (keep `build_output_is_refused` as is).

xtask/tests/policy.rs: split `boundary_scan` into `scan_words` and `scan_fragments` (keeping `boundary_scan` as their union, so the admission-agreement test is unchanged). Add `claim_quote_exempt(path)` (exactly `studies/<one id>/claims.json`), `without_claim_quotes(text)` (serde_json parse, collect `sources[].quote` strings, replace `"quote": <literal>` for those literals with an empty string, one line in and one line out) and `boundary_scan_file(path, text)` (words on the blanked text, fragments on the raw text). Use it in `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where`. Add tests for each case in the criterion 4 demonstration, planting the word and the fragment with `.concat()` from split parts. Grep the file for the banned words before finishing.
crates/athena-cap-study/Cargo.toml: add `tempfile.workspace = true` under [dev-dependencies]. Cargo.lock: add "tempfile" after "serde_json" in the athena-cap-study entry.

producer.md: rewrite with the existing rules kept and these added, in priority order: start every claim text with `[mechanism]` or `[prose-only]`; give the full pinned SHA; no placeholders (UNRESOLVED, not examined); a guard that does not exist is `none`, never checked by code; change only one `studies/<id>/` and CHANGELOG.md; a claim quote stays verbatim even if it holds a scanned word, since the scan skips claim quotes only. Offset the additions by tightening: shorten the intro to one clause, drop '(read-only)', merge the tag rule into the claim bullet, merge the two last bullets, shorten the rationale-card and `contradicts` bullets. Net growth must stay within about 75 bytes of the current 1019. Do not write the scan's word list in the prompt, and avoid the text 'agent-reference'. Then run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` and `cargo test -p athena-context`; the budgets test must pass with docs/system-facts.md unmodified. If it fails reporting a larger producer value, tighten further, dropping the quote clause first; if the clause is dropped, say so in the CHANGELOG entry. Do not edit docs/system-facts.md.

CHANGELOG.md: add the entry under [Unreleased] / ### Changed, without writing the banned words. It covers the per-study validation, the prompt conventions, the admission rule, the boundary exemption for claim quotes, the note that a study of a repository with several studies fails the kept test when its pin has the same URL and a different SHA than ATHENA_PIN_*, and, if dropped from the prompt, the claim-quote gap.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` (or the crate tests named in the demonstrations: `cargo test -p athena-cap-study`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`, `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`). Where pinned-source/ and ATHENA_PIN_* are present, confirm the log shows firstmate fully validated. Run `git status` to confirm nothing under studies/, no athena.toml and no docs/system-facts.md changed.

risks.risk: The ATHENA_PIN_* variables may not reach the test process, so full validation would silently not run, which is weaker than today's behavior of validating whenever pinned-source/ exists.
risks.mitigation: The kept test prints which studies were fully validated and which were convention-only. The hermetic test (tree rebuilt from citations) runs the full-validation route in every checkout. The Host open question asks.

risks.risk: The reconstructed tree is built from the study's own citations, so it cannot show that the real tree holds the quotes.
risks.mitigation: The test's doc comment says so. Only the mounted-tree path proves the quotes; criterion 1's mounted command covers it on a host with pinned-source/, which this job's verifier cannot see.

risks.risk: Several single-line ranges in firstmate's claims.json are shared by different quotes (docs/configuration.md 357-357 and 1088-1088, AGENTS.md 234-234, docs/agent-control.md 131-131, bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh 49-49, bin/fm-spawn.sh 3165-3165), so a one-quote-per-line tree collides. A quote containing a newline could also shift later lines.
risks.mitigation: synthetic_tree joins every quote beginning on a line with a space and pads to the highest end line. The test asserts `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` are empty on the rebuilt tree before comparing with validation.json, so any placement fault is reported by claim id instead of as a diff. A multi-line quote is placed at its start line with its own newlines; the same pre-check catches a shifted range.

risks.risk: The rewritten study prompt grows past 1043 tokens, the recorded largest producer set, and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails; docs/system-facts.md is not a deliverable so it cannot be edited.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 sets a budget of about 75 bytes net growth over the current 1019 bytes. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` after each edit and tightens until it passes with the facts file unchanged. Order of dropping if it will not fit: the claim-quote clause first (recorded as a gap in CHANGELOG), then wording of existing bullets. If still too large, the producer stops and reports it (third open question) instead of editing the facts file.

risks.risk: Study jobs that legitimately touch another path (for example a shared doc) are now refused.
risks.mitigation: The brief expects about 5% newly refused readings. The violation detail names the allowed set (one studies/<id>/ plus CHANGELOG.md) so the producer can fix the change in one retry; the prompt now states the rule.

risks.risk: A studied system's words in a rationale-card quote, or in a claim's own prose, still fail the boundary scan.
risks.mitigation: That is what the request asks for: only claim quotes are exempt. Raised as a user question.

risks.risk: With several studies of one repository, the same-URL-different-SHA failure can fire for a study the job did not pick.
risks.mitigation: The request's rule is kept; the failure names the study id and both SHAs so the cause is clear, the conflict is recorded in the CHANGELOG entry, and the fourth open question asks the user whether to relax it.

demonstrations.method: Run the study crate tests. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` calls `check_studies(studies root, env pair read from ATHENA_PIN_URL/ATHENA_PIN_SHA, mount ../../pinned-source if it is a directory)` and prints one line per study: 'fully validated' or 'conventions only'. `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations` passes the study's own URL and SHA as the env pair and a `synthetic_tree` as the mount; it first asserts `bad_citation` and `quote_mismatch` are empty on that tree, then asserts `validate()` equals validation.json. `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too` builds a temp studies root holding the firstmate copy and a renamed copy with an untagged claim. The mounted-case command for a checkout that has pinned-source/ is: `ATHENA_PIN_URL=<repository_url in studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json> ATHENA_PIN_SHA=<sha in the same file> cargo test -p athena-cap-study rules::tests -- --nocapture`; it should print 'firstmate-work-handling: fully validated'. This job's verifier cannot see that case (no pinned-source/ in the snapshot, and no code in the snapshot sets the pair); it must rely on the rebuilt-tree test for the validation route.
demonstrations.observes: With no ATHENA_PIN_* set, every studies/*/ passes the conventions and the output says 'conventions only'. The rebuilt-tree test passes: validate() on the tree built from the study's citations equals validation.json, and the second-directory test fails naming the second directory and its claim id. In the mounted case (host only) the kept test runs validate() against the real tree and the printed line says fully validated.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the loop skipped a directory, the second-directory test would not name the bad claim. If the matching branch never called `validate()`, a tampered validation.json copy would pass the rebuilt-tree test. If `synthetic_tree` collided on shared single-line ranges, the pre-check on bad-citation or quote-mismatch would name the claim and fail the test.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `validate()` and the rules exist (rules.rs). New test-module functions `check_study`, `check_studies`, `Loaded::read(dir)` and `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` are added by plan steps 1-4. Fixtures: the real studies/ directory, `tempfile::TempDir` copies, and a `MountedTree` (exists in the rules.rs test module at ~1412, generalized in step 1) over a real or rebuilt root; root, env pair and mount are injected as arguments. The doubles hold no rule logic: validation, `wrong_sha`, `bad_citation`, `quote_mismatch` and the conventions run the real code.

demonstrations.method: The test copies the first study directory into a TempDir (copy helper, step 4), edits its JSON with serde_json and calls `check_study`. (a) Set claims[0].text to untagged prose: a problem containing that claim id and 'enforcement'. (b) Set transitions[0].guard to "none" and guard_evaluated_by to "code": a problem naming the transition id. (c) Set claims[0].sources[0].sha to a different 40-hex: a problem naming the claim id. (d) Leave the copy unchanged and pass an env pair with the pin's URL and a different SHA, with a temp dir as mount: a problem naming the study id and both SHAs. A control (unmodified copy, env unset) returns no problems; a last case (env unset, a changed quote) returns no problems, showing conventions only.
demonstrations.observes: Four asserts of the form `problems.iter().any(|p| p.contains(<id>))` plus the control returning empty. Failure strings begin with the offending id (claim, transition or study).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the tag check, the none-guard check, the SHA check or the pin-mismatch check were removed, the matching case would return an empty list and its assertion would fail. If a message omitted the id, `contains(id)` would fail.
demonstrations.seam: `check_study(dir, pin_env, mount)` is added in step 3. Fixtures are `tempfile::TempDir` copies of the real study, with `tempfile` added to dev-dependencies in step 7. The pin env pair and mount are injected as arguments. The conventions run the real `wrong_sha` rule with a `NoTree` lookup (added in step 1) that only supplies absent git answers.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in lib.rs call `Study.admit(&ChangeList, &job_config())`. Cases: (1) studies/a/claims.json, studies/a/model.json and CHANGELOG.md gives none. (2) studies/a/claims.json and studies/b/claims.json gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming a and b. (3) studies/a/claims.json and docs/x.md gives one `study-outside-directory` violation with path docs/x.md. (4) CHANGELOG.md alone gives none. (5) docs/CHANGELOG.md, studies/x, studies/a/../b/c and a deleted file under a second directory are refused. (6) target/debug/x with studies/s1/claims.json gives exactly one violation, the existing build-output case. Input forms (path shapes) map to these cases. athena-core's refusal_corpus covers request-reading checks and has no case for change-path admission (grep of refusal_corpus.rs for admit, ChangeList and studies/ found none), so no corpus case is added; `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` can be run as a further check that the reading corpus is unchanged, and I cite no result for it.
demonstrations.observes: Violations returned by `admit()` equal the expected rule names and paths for every case; the existing `build_output_is_refused` still passes. The tightening is intended: roughly 5% of study readings are expected to be newly refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old admit, the two-directory and outside-file cases return zero violations, so the assertions on count and rule name fail.
demonstrations.seam: `Study::admit` exists (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:112), called by crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs:164 and run/mod.rs:783 through the `Capability` trait. The seam is a directly built `ChangeList` and the existing `job_config()` fixture (lib.rs:132). The helper `study_dir_of(path) -> Option<&str>` is added in step 5 and called by the real code, not faked.

demonstrations.method: New tests call the new `boundary_scan_file(path, text)` (step 6). Claims text is built with `serde_json::json!` and `to_string_pretty`. The planted word and the machine-path fragment are built with `.concat()` from split parts, as in `the_boundary_scanner_flags_a_planted_term` (policy.rs:187). Cases: a banned word in a claim's source quote in studies/s/claims.json gives no hit; the same word in the claim's `text` gives a hit; in studies/s/findings.json or studies/s/notes.md prose gives a hit; the same claims JSON at docs/x/claims.json, crates/x/claims.json or studies/a/b/claims.json gives a hit; a machine-path fragment inside a claim quote gives a hit; a word in a rationale-card quote in studies/s/rationales.json gives a hit; invalid JSON in claims.json exempts nothing. `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` calls the new function over tracked files. A Grep of xtask/tests/policy.rs for each banned word from the list there (list not written in this plan) must find no match.

open_questions: Host: Are ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA set in the environment of study jobs' producer, verifier and cargo checks? A search of this snapshot (rust, toml, md) finds no code that sets them, and athena.toml's [capabilities.study.env] (out of scope) lists only CARGO_TARGET_DIR and CARGO_TERM_COLOR. If unset, the kept test checks conventions only and full validation against the mounted tree never runs by default; the rebuilt-tree test still exercises the route.

User: Should rationale-card source quotes in rationales.json be exempt from the boundary scan as well? The request names only the quote fields of a study's claims, so the plan exempts only claims.json; a studied system's own words in a rationale quote would still fail the scan.

User: If the conventions cannot fit in the 25-token (about 75-byte) growth the study prompt may have without moving the recorded largest producer set, may the producer update the `- budget producer:` line in docs/system-facts.md, which is not a listed deliverable? The plan assumes no, tightens wording, and drops the claim-quote clause (recording the gap in CHANGELOG.md) before anything else.

The request's rule makes every other study of that URL with a different SHA fail the kept test. The plan keeps the rule as asked; should it instead skip, not fail, a same-URL study whose SHA differs, once the pinning change can pass the study id?
